sourceInformation.tech: HTML5, JavaScript, my-3D2dge v0.89.1 (8ecc2f6); AI Hub protocol v1/client v1.4.0 (35a1047); Web Audio; reproducible Node assembly
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original code-drawn shaded pixel puppets and jewel-colored alien garden dioramas
sourceInformation.animation: Native Blob rigs, continuous procedural locomotion and expression, pixel effects and chain path sampling
sourceInformation.audio: Original synthesized motif with five arrangements, effects and gibberish voices; separate music/effects/voice buses; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub authoritative shared-world co-op for 1–2 players, including a non-playing authority; standalone couch co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless deterministic rules and native draw checks; ordinary-command solo/co-op and controller campaign endings; Playwright 1.63 Chromium and WebKit phone/tablet stand-ins; OfflineAudioContext; official Hub normal/impaired/server/host-departure scenarios (150ms latency,50ms jitter,5% loss). No FPS target, physical device or human listening claim.
sourceInformation.research: Read original text and illustrated manual; inspected actual cover/rules pages and 18–39s of gameplay footage frames from https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=whykVbhZD8c. Original audio unknown. Packaging and magazine direct fetch unavailable. Full URLs/observations in development artifacts/research.md.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Ubuntu 26.04 Linux on WSL2

testingFeedback: 30 unique product issues caught by testing and integration review, corrected before delivery; ledger distinguishes test-fixture mistakes.
1 potential game-breaking corrupt-save crash path, fixed by validated snapshot restoration. No fresh-profile campaign blocker remained.
A full assembled-artifact campaign driven only through a standard gamepad input stand-in, plus shared-world authority/replica assertions under packet loss and host departure.
The initial Input.feed multitouch check only exercised gestures, not the native floating stick, and gave false failures. Replaced it with actual Chromium multitouch pointer events.
engineFeedback: The native shaded pixel helpers, expressive Blob rigs, controller menus and separate synthesis buses fit the game without external assets.
I initially expected Input.feed to drive floating sticks; its gesture/zone behavior required actual browser pointer sequences for that test. Engine globals also differ from a CommonJS return value.
The deterministic wrap-aware chain simulation, explicit collision order, campaign checkpoints and authoritative shared-world adapter.
Keeping the full maze and native menus readable across TV and portrait layouts, while separating simulation cells from projected pixels.
None. The pristine engine is unchanged; game-specific topology, immediate reversal, Hub and menu adapters are authored modules.
First-class paired grid edges and a documented shared-world input/snapshot adapter would reduce custom integration.
promptFeedback: The precise source mechanics, finite five-garden campaign, accessible editor and evidence-based reporting gave the game a clear identity.
The first-human-run target of 12–18 minutes cannot be verified without human playtesting; optimal bots and stand-ins establish different evidence.
Making the same rules, controls and outcomes work across solo, couch co-op, a non-playing Hub authority, tools and a self-contained HTML.
Order requirements by acceptance priority and explicitly separate automated evidence from human pacing, listening and physical-device checks.

aiHub.name: K.C.’s Krazy Wrap Party
aiHub.tagline: Nibble the tail. Mind the teeth.
aiHub.description: A very hungry garden caper on Venus. Chase glowing tails, dodge horned heads, plant sneaky snacks and share the mischief across five original gardens and a maze workshop.
aiHub.controls: WASD/arrows or left stick/D-pad: move; Space/Cross (Xbox A): plant; Escape/Options: pause; mouse click to walk/plant; touch drag + PLANT.
